rule: Body text contrast ≥ 4.5:1; large text (≥24px or 19px bold) ≥ 3:1; UI components/graphics ≥ 3:1.
anti: Gray-on-gray, low-contrast placeholder text used as labels.

rule: Every interactive element has a visible focus ring (2px, ≥3:1 against its background). Never remove focus outlines without a stronger replacement.
anti: outline:none with no substitute — keyboard users get lost.

rule: All functionality is reachable and operable by keyboard alone, in a logical tab order; no keyboard traps.
anti: Custom widgets that only respond to mouse/hover.

rule: Icon-only buttons carry an accessible name (aria-label or visually-hidden text). Images have alt; decorative images use empty alt or aria-hidden.
anti: Icon buttons with no name; alt text describing 'image'.

rule: Interactive targets ≥ 44×44px (WCAG 2.5.5 / Apple HIG), with ≥8px spacing between adjacent targets.
anti: Tiny tap targets crammed together on mobile.

rule: Honor prefers-reduced-motion: disable or reduce non-essential animation; never gate content behind motion.
anti: Parallax and autoplay that ignore the OS reduced-motion setting.

rule: Do not require a cognitive test (memorizing, transcribing) to authenticate; allow paste and password managers (WCAG 2.2 Accessible Authentication).
anti: Blocking paste in password/OTP fields.

rule: Every tap/click gives feedback within 100ms (pressed state, ripple, or optimistic update). No 0ms silent state changes.
anti: Button that looks dead until the network returns.

rule: Show loading state for anything >300ms: skeletons for content, spinners for actions, disabled+label for buttons.
anti: Frozen UI with no signal that work is happening.

rule: Never hide essential actions behind hover only — touch devices have no hover. Provide a persistent or tap-revealed path.
anti: Row actions that only appear on :hover.

rule: Destructive actions need friction: confirm dialog, undo window, or type-to-confirm. Prefer undo over confirm for reversible ops.
anti: One-tap permanent delete with no undo.

rule: Serve WebP/AVIF with width/height set; lazy-load below-the-fold images; use responsive srcset.
anti: Full-res PNG hero shipped to phones.

rule: Reserve space for images, ads, embeds and fonts to keep CLS < 0.1; use aspect-ratio and font-display:swap with metric-adjusted fallbacks.
anti: Content jumping as images and fonts load.

rule: Virtualize lists beyond ~100 rows; paginate or windowing rather than rendering thousands of nodes.
anti: Rendering a 5000-row table into the DOM at once.

rule: Keep the main thread free: debounce/throttle input handlers, move heavy work off the render path, avoid layout thrash (batch reads then writes).
anti: Scroll handler doing synchronous layout every frame.

rule: Commit to one aesthetic and apply it consistently — one radius scale, one shadow system, one spacing scale. Consistency reads as craft.
anti: Mixing flat and skeuomorphic, three radii, random shadows.

rule: Use a single SVG icon set (one weight/family). Never use emoji as UI icons.
anti: Emoji sprinkled as functional icons.

rule: Express hierarchy with one consistent elevation language (border OR shadow OR surface tint) — pick one primary and use it everywhere.
anti: Heavy drop-shadows on a flat/brutalist layout.

rule: One accent color carries interaction and emphasis. Everything else is neutral. Restraint reads as premium.
anti: Four competing brand colors on one screen.

rule: Design mobile-first with fluid breakpoints; content reflows, no fixed-px containers that overflow small screens.
anti: Desktop-only layout that forces horizontal scroll on phones.

rule: No unintended horizontal scroll; set a 16px side gutter minimum; test at 320px width.
anti: A wide element pushing the viewport sideways.

rule: Set viewport meta correctly and never disable pinch-zoom (no maximum-scale=1, no user-scalable=no).
anti: Disabling zoom 'for design reasons'.

rule: Cap body text measure at 60-75 characters; center long-form in a readable column rather than full-bleed.
anti: Paragraphs running the full 1440px width.

rule: Use a consistent grid/spacing scale (e.g. 4px base) for every gap and inset; no magic numbers.
anti: Ad-hoc 13px/17px/23px paddings.

rule: Base body ≥16px, line-height ~1.5; never set body copy below 12px.
anti: 11px body text to fit more in.

rule: Use a modular type scale (e.g. 1.2-1.333 ratio) with a limited step count; enforce clear H1>H2>H3 hierarchy.
anti: Six heading sizes all within 2px of each other.

rule: Tighten tracking on large display (-0.01 to -0.03em); leave body at default. Balance headings (text-wrap:balance) and avoid orphans.
anti: Loose tracking on huge headings; a one-word orphan line.

rule: Drive text color from semantic tokens (text/muted/inverse), not raw hex per component.
anti: Hardcoded #333 scattered across components.

rule: Motion must convey meaning (spatial continuity, causality, state) — not decorate. If it does not aid understanding, cut it.
anti: Everything spins/bounces on load.

rule: Use context-aware timing: micro (100-150ms), UI transitions (200-300ms), larger moves (300-500ms). Not one duration for everything.
anti: Every transition set to a flat 500ms.

rule: Exits are faster than entrances; use ease-out for enters, ease-in for exits. Springs for interactive/dragged elements.
anti: Slow linear fades that make the UI feel sluggish.

rule: Animate only transform and opacity for 60fps; never animate width/height/top/left in hot paths (they trigger layout).
anti: Animating width/height on scroll.

rule: Every field has a persistent visible label; placeholders are hints, never the label.
anti: Placeholder-only fields that lose their label on input.

rule: Validate inline near the field on blur/submit; show the error adjacent with a clear fix, not only a summary at the top.
anti: Generic 'error occurred' banner at page top.

rule: Error messages state what is wrong and how to fix it, in plain language; never blame the user or use codes alone.
anti: 'Invalid input' with no guidance.

rule: Ask only what is needed now; use progressive disclosure and sensible defaults; group related fields.
anti: A 30-field form on first contact.

rule: Use correct input types/inputmode/autocomplete so mobile keyboards and password managers help the user.
anti: type=text for email/phone/number.

rule: Keep primary nav shallow and predictable; surface the most-used destinations, hide the rest under clear grouping.
anti: A flat mega-menu of 30 equal links.

rule: Mobile bottom nav ≤5 items; put the primary destinations there, not everything.
anti: Seven crammed bottom-tab icons.

rule: Back must be predictable; preserve scroll and state on return; support deep links to any meaningful view.
anti: Back that dumps the user to home and loses state.

rule: Always show where the user is (active state, breadcrumbs for depth) so they can orient and escape.
anti: No active indicator; user can't tell the current section.

rule: Never rely on color alone to distinguish series; add direct labels, patterns, or shapes; ensure colorblind-safe palettes.
anti: Red/green lines indistinguishable to colorblind users.

rule: Provide readable legends and tooltips; prefer direct labeling over a distant legend when few series.
anti: A legend the user must map back and forth to read.

rule: Start bar-chart axes at zero; do not truncate to exaggerate differences; label units.
anti: Truncated y-axis inflating a tiny difference.

rule: Match chart type to intent: trend→line, comparison→bar, part-of-whole→stacked/treemap (not pie for many slices), distribution→histogram/box.
anti: A 12-slice pie chart.
